statement.p: Find \int_C\vec F\cdot d\vec r where C is a circle of radius 3 in the plane x+y+z=4, centered at (2,1,1) and oriented clockwise when viewed from the origin, if \vec F = 5y\vec i - 2x\vec j + 2\mathopen{}\left(y-x\right)\vec k

static.solution: \mbox{curl }\vec F = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} \vec i \amp \vec j \amp \vec k\\ \frac{\partial}{\partial x}\ \amp \ \frac{\partial}{\partial y} \ \amp \ \frac{\partial}{\partial z}\\ 5y \amp -2x \amp 2\mathopen{}\left(y-x\right) \end{array} \right| = 2\vec i + 2\vec j -7 \vec k, writing S for the disk in the plane enclosed by the circle, Stokes' Theorem gives \int_C\vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_S\mbox{curl }\vec F\cdot d\vec A = \int_S(2\vec i + 2\vec j -7 \vec k)\cdot d\vec A. Now d\vec A = \vec n\,dA, where \vec n is the unit vector perpendicular to the plane and dA an area element on the plane, so \vec n = \frac1{\sqrt3}(\vec i + \vec j + \vec k), and \int_C\vec F\,d\vec r = \int_S(2\vec i+2\vec j -7\vec k)\cdot \frac{\vec i+\vec j+\vec k}{\sqrt{3}}\,dA = \int_S \frac{-3}{\sqrt 3}\,dA = \frac{-3}{\sqrt 3}\mbox{ Area of circle} = \frac{-27\pi}{\sqrt{3}}.
